title: GPU capacity congestion matrix — 2026-03-24
description: Rolling daily export formatted as a congestion matrix to help prioritize pool-level mitigation. Combines 1d average/peak utilization, headroom, orphaned sockets, and a subjective congestion score for quick triage.
scope: All production clusters (NA/EU/APAC) sampled at 00:00 UTC for 2026-03-24. Focus on pools used by Hosted API and Dedicated customers; private deployment pools excluded unless flagged.
methodology: Samples are pulled from /monitoring/api/v1/gpu-summaries aggregated by cluster->pool. Avg/peak are 24h rolling averages and 99th-percentile peaks respectively. Headroom percent = (available_capacity / total_capacity) * 100. Orphaned sockets flagged where pool_id has active nodes but no route assignments in last 48h.
observation_summary: Overall fleet average utilization is moderate, but several small pools in APAC show repeated peak spikes and low headroom. NA large pools have consistent tail-latency workloads driving peak utilization; some Dedicated pools approaching <10% headroom which is a risk for canary rollouts.

key_findings: 1) Two critical pools (cl-fra-02:dedicated-eu-1 and cl-sin-01:embed-inference) have <10% headroom and recurring 99p spikes — immediate mitigation required. 2) Multiple small APAC pools contain orphaned sockets; a cleanup pass would free modest capacity. 3) NA webgen-small shows sustained evening peaks; consider auto-burst policy or prewarmed warm nodes. 4) Several dev/ephemeral pools can be scheduled for drain windows to shift load during high-demand events.
recommended_actions:
- Open high-priority capacity incident for cl-fra-02 and cl-sin-01 (INF-4287).
- Schedule orphaned-socket cleanup job (script: infra/maintenance/clear-orphans) for 2026-03-26.
- Add conditional burst policy to webgen-small: +2 nodes during 00:03–08:00 UTC.
- Run 48h target monitoring on dedicated-na-2 and webgen-small; if 99p > 85% repeatedly, escalate to capacity procurement.
- Re-evaluate placement of background batch processors to embed-inference where headroom available.

visualization_notes: Recommended UI: congestion matrix heatmap keyed by congestion_score with ability to filter by region and pool size. Add sparklines for 7d trend per row and drilldown to node-level utilization.
final_comment: This export aims to be a lightweight triage sheet for on-call and capacity planners; not a replacement for the canonical daily capacity report but quicker to scan for hotspots.
